::: {.callout-note .summary appearance="simple" icon=false}
## At a glance
::: {.summary-grid}
Question
:   How does vehicle weight relate to fuel efficiency, and does it differ by transmission?

Data
:   `mtcars` · 32 cars, 1974 *Motor Trend*

Methods
:   OLS with a weight × transmission interaction

Finding
:   Heavier cars get fewer MPG, and the penalty is steeper for manual transmissions.
:::
:::

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(knitr)

df <- transform(mtcars, transmission = factor(am, labels = c("Automatic", "Manual")))
```
:::


## Model


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt * transmission, data = df)

tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "OLS estimates (outcome: miles per gallon)")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


Table: OLS estimates (outcome: miles per gallon)

|term                  | estimate| std.error| statistic| p.value| conf.low| conf.high|
|:---------------------|--------:|---------:|---------:|-------:|--------:|---------:|

|wt                    |    -3.79|      0.79|     -4.82|       0|    -5.40|     -2.18|
|transmissionManual    |    14.88|      4.26|      3.49|       0|     6.14|     23.61|
|wt:transmissionManual |    -5.30|      1.44|     -3.67|       0|    -8.26|     -2.34|


:::
:::


## Visualization


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(df, aes(wt, mpg, colour = transmission, fill = transmission)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", alpha = 0.15) +
  labs(x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)", y = "Miles per gallon", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

::: {.takeaways}
- Each additional 1,000 lbs is associated with a drop in MPG for both groups, with a larger slope for manual cars.
